solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: US student to be inquisitive about revolutionary Oxford course

indicators.note: about means the first piece goes round the second

parts.note: to pry is to be nosy or inquisitive

indicators.note: revolutionary means the course's letters turn right round, read backwards

parts.note: PPE is Philosophy, Politics and Economics, a famous Oxford degree course

explanation.surface: Someone nosily questions an American student about a radical Oxford degree.
explanation.walkthrough: PPE (Philosophy, Politics and Economics) is Oxford's famous degree for future politicians; 'revolutionary' turns it round before 'about' wraps the prying round it.
explanation.definitionFit: Preppy describes, and in US slang names, a student from an expensive private prep school.

clue.text: Beat poet?

definitions.meaning: to beat repeatedly, as with a fist or hammer

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a Beat poet such as Ginsberg; instead 'Beat' and 'poet' are separate definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: To pound is to strike hard; Ezra Pound wrote The Cantos.

clue.text: Short-lived recording with Elgar's 1st and Mahler transcription

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record

indicators.note: a transcription rearranges music for other forces, so these letters are rearranged
1st means only the opening letter of Elgar's is taken

explanation.surface: A recording pairs an Elgar first symphony with a Mahler arrangement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transcription', a musical term fitting the surface, signals that the composer's name and Elgar's initial are reshuffled together.
explanation.definitionFit: Ephemeral things last only a day or so: fleeting, transient.

clue.text: Loaf and meat spread

definitions.meaning: loaf is slang for the head, as in 'use your loaf'
a paste of meat or liver spread on toast

explanation.walkthrough: 'Loaf' suggests bread to go with the spread; it is British slang for the head.
explanation.definitionFit: Pate is an old word for the top of the head; pâté is a savoury paste.

clue.text: Meet to chat: that's good for society

indicators.note: for here means one letter stands in place of the other: G replaces S

parts.note: to converse is to chat

explanation.surface: A sociable meeting for a chat, praised as good for community life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's good for society' reads as praise; in fact G goes in place of S.
explanation.definitionFit: Lines or people that converge come together at one point, so they meet.

clue.text: Republican central to current problem causing scandal

indicators.note: central to puts the letter in the middle of the other piece

parts.note: a power outage is a problem with the electric current

explanation.surface: A Republican at the heart of a political problem causes a scandal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'current' looks like 'present-day' but means electricity.
explanation.definitionFit: A scandal is a public outrage, something causing shock and indignation.

clue.text: Liverpudlian singer introduced by Virginia and Edward lacked confidence

indicators.note: introduced by means the singer comes after the state, which leads in

parts.note: VA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Virginia
Cilla Black, the singer and TV presenter from Liverpool
Ted is a familiar form of Edward

explanation.surface: A Liverpool singer, presented by Virginia and Edward, felt nervous.
explanation.walkthrough: Cilla Black was a 1960s Liverpool singer, later a British TV host.
explanation.definitionFit: To vacillate is to waver, unable to decide: a sign of lacking confidence.

clue.text: Cash crop, you say? Not so

indicators.note: you say means the word for the crop is spoken and spelt as another syllable

parts.note: rye is a cereal crop
no is a denial: not so

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a cash crop is meant, and is told no.
explanation.walkthrough: Rhino is old British slang for money.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhino is a dated slang term for money, especially ready cash.

clue.text: Cockney boss heading off after packing gun

indicators.note: packing means the trimmed word holds the gun inside it
heading off removes the first letter of the word

parts.note: a leader is the boss
the Sten was a British submachine gun

explanation.surface: A Cockney mob boss leaves after concealing a gun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading off' beheads the boss and 'packing' (carrying a gun, in gangster slang) wraps it round the weapon. A Cockney is a working-class Londoner from the East End.
explanation.definitionFit: An East Ender comes from the East End of London, Cockney territory.

clue.text: Most of the people in old Balkan land

indicators.note: most of drops the final letter of the next word

parts.note: a race is a people

explanation.surface: Most of the population lived in an ancient Balkan country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Most of' trims THE to TH.
explanation.definitionFit: Thrace was an ancient region of the south-east Balkans, now split between Greece, Bulgaria and Turkey.

clue.text: Free university tuition at last? There's a problem with that

indicators.note: at last takes only the final letter of tuition

parts.note: a hitch is a snag or problem

explanation.surface: Someone queries free university tuition, objecting that there is a snag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Free' looks like an adjective about the fees; it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To unhitch something is to unfasten it, setting it free.

clue.text: With show of diplomacy, regularly discuss strategy

parts.note: tact is diplomacy shown in dealing with people

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of discuss

explanation.surface: Diplomats routinely discuss strategy, tactfully.
explanation.definitionFit: Tactics and strategy are both plans for gaining an end, near-synonyms in loose use.

clue.text: Far from shiny English coin

parts.note: dim means dull, far from shiny

explanation.surface: A dull, tarnished English coin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'English coin' looks like one phrase, but the dime is American.
explanation.definitionFit: A dime is a US ten-cent coin.

clue.text: Liz unsteadily carries a container with single dish

indicators.note: carries means the jumbled name holds the next pieces inside it
unsteadily means the letters of the name wobble into a new order

parts.note: a bag is a container
one means single

explanation.surface: Liz, wobbling, carries a container with a single dish in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unsteadily' jumbles the name to ZLI, and 'carries' has that hold the article and the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Zabaglione is an Italian dessert of whipped egg yolks, sugar and Marsala.

clue.text: Ritual in church, one almoner organised

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

indicators.note: organised means these letters are put into a new order

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: A church ritual arranged by one of its almoners.
explanation.walkthrough: An almoner was a church officer who gave out alms.
explanation.definitionFit: Ceremonial as a noun means the formal rites of an occasion: ritual.

clue.text: To keep going is hard after benefit cut

indicators.note: after puts the second piece following the first
cut docks the last letter from the word

parts.note: a perk is a benefit of a job
severe means hard or harsh

explanation.surface: Persisting is tough once welfare benefit has been cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'benefit' suggests welfare; here it is a job perk, and 'cut' drops its K.
explanation.definitionFit: To persevere is to persist, carrying on despite difficulty.

clue.text: Send attachment without content? Insert latest copy

indicators.note: Insert means the latest news goes inside the word for send

parts.note: to post is to send by mail
hot means very latest, as in hot news

indicators.note: without content means only the outside letters of attachment remain

explanation.surface: An email instruction: send an empty attachment, then insert the latest copy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Insert' and 'without content' read like computer instructions; they put the latest news inside the mailing word and strip attachment to its outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A photostat is a photographic copy of a document, from an early copier brand.

clue.text: Tony, perhaps, embarrassed having week away

indicators.note: away means the abbreviation is taken out of the longer word

parts.note: awkward means uncomfortable or embarrassed

explanation.surface: Tony is embarrassed after taking a week off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tony' looks like a person's name; it is the Broadway theatre prize.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tony is a theatre prize, one example of an honour of that kind.

clue.text: One wild cat endlessly confronts another in sunny spot

indicators.note: confronts puts the first piece facing, in front of, the second
endlessly removes both the first and last letters

parts.note: a panther is one kind of wild cat
another wild cat: a lion

explanation.surface: A wild cat faces down another in a patch of sunshine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' trims PANTHER to ANTHE.
explanation.definitionFit: An anthelion is a bright halo spot seen in the sky opposite the sun.

clue.text: See dog without lead jump

indicators.note: without lead removes the leading letter

parts.note: a collie is a breed of sheepdog

explanation.surface: Look at the dog jump once off its leash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lead' suggests a dog's leash; it means the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An ollie is a skateboarding trick in which rider and board leap into the air.

clue.text: Craftsman's moan: tenant has blocked off entrance

parts.note: to carp is to complain or moan

indicators.note: blocked off entrance means the word's first letter, its way in, is shut off

parts.note: a renter is a tenant

explanation.surface: A builder complains that a tenant has blocked the entrance.
explanation.definitionFit: A carpenter is a skilled woodworker, a classic craftsman.

clue.text: Initially, congregation unanimously values members of clergy

indicators.note: Initially takes the first letter of each of the next two words

parts.note: rates means values, as in assessing worth

explanation.surface: A congregation unanimously values its clergy.
explanation.definitionFit: Curates are assistant parish clergy in the Church of England.

clue.text: Bug scampered over wild animal standing up

indicators.note: over in a down clue puts the first piece above the second

parts.note: ran means scampered

indicators.note: standing up in a down clue means the animal's letters read upwards, backwards

parts.note: an elk is a large wild deer

explanation.surface: An insect scurried over a wild animal standing on its hind legs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bug' looks like an insect that scampered; it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To bug is to annoy; to rankle is to cause lasting irritation.

clue.text: Display of emotion for Parisian during trip

indicators.note: during means the French word goes inside the trip

parts.note: an outing is a trip
a Parisian would say pour, the French for for

explanation.surface: A Parisian shows emotion during an outing.
explanation.definitionFit: An outpouring is a sudden unrestrained expression of feeling.

clue.text: Strike that has union members protesting, initially

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of each of the preceding words

explanation.surface: A strike begins with union members protesting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strike' suggests industrial action; it means a blow.
explanation.definitionFit: To thump is to strike hard with a fist.

clue.text: Money illegally obtained from raffle proceeds sent back

indicators.note: sent back says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Takings from a raffle, embezzled and later returned.
explanation.walkthrough: Inside 'raffle proceeds' sits FLEP, which 'sent back' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: Pelf is money, especially wealth gained dishonestly.

clue.text: N Dakota city: a long way to travel

parts.note: far means a long way
to go is to travel

explanation.surface: A North Dakota city is a long way to travel.
explanation.definitionFit: Fargo is the largest city in North Dakota.

clue.text: Scourges regularly making you —

indicators.note: regularly takes alternate letters of scourges, starting from the first

explanation.surface: Whips used repeatedly leave you, as the dash invites you to supply, painful.
explanation.walkthrough: The dash leaves the answer to finish the sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: Repeated whipping leaves you aching and tender: in pain.

clue.text: One travelling to historical city is needing extra time

parts.note: Ur was an ancient city of Mesopotamia

explanation.surface: A traveller heading to an ancient city needs more time.
explanation.definitionFit: A tourist is someone travelling for pleasure.

clue.text: More bananas, look: old and terribly ripe

parts.note: lo is an old word for look

indicators.note: terribly means these letters are badly jumbled

explanation.surface: Look: the old bananas are terribly overripe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bananas' looks like fruit to match 'ripe', but means crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: Bananas is slang for crazy, and loopy means crazy too, so loopier is more so.

clue.text: A1 partially closed? Proceed round outer parts of capital

parts.note: a door pulled to is almost but not fully closed

indicators.note: round means the verb goes around the other letters

parts.note: to pass is to proceed

indicators.note: outer parts of takes the first and last letters of capital

explanation.surface: A road sign: the A1 partly closed, so drive round the edge of the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: The A1 is the main road north from London; here A1 means excellent.
explanation.definitionFit: A1 means first-rate, the very best quality.

clue.text: Sorted out early part of play for broadcast

indicators.note: for broadcast means the words are spoken on air, giving a sound-alike

parts.note: scene two comes near the start of a play

explanation.surface: An early scene of a play was sorted out for radio.
explanation.definitionFit: Something seen to has been dealt with or attended to.
